To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adsorption capacity of phenol on polymeric resins depends on the microporosities and surface chemistry of these adsorbents.
the adsorption of polar phenol on the four kinds of poly(styrene-co-divinylbenzene) resins is strongly influenced by both the microporosities and the surface polarities of the polymeric resin.
the adsorptive properties for phenol of polymeric resines are strongly dependent on their micropore structure and surface polarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the surface chemistry of poly(styrene-divinylbenzene) resins on adsorption of phenolic compounds.

the effects of microporosity on adsorptive property of the polymeric resions, and it provides a useful reference for the design and synthesis of new adsorbent materials with high adsorption performance.
the effects of the chemical surface and micropore structure on adsorptive performance toward phenol of the polymeric adsorbent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the well-developed micporosity and the strong polar surface of polymeric resine would be favorable for the adsorption of polar phenol.
the adsorption of organic molecules on polymeric resins is not simply a function of their microporosities, but is also strongly dependent on their surface chemistry.

adsorption of organic pollutants on the polymeric adsorbent depends greatly on its microporosity, surface chemistry and the nature of organic pollutants, and the microporosities and surface chemistries of polymeric resin should be taken into consideration in the selection of adsorption materials for the removal of organic pollutants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microporovosity and the strong polarity of adsorbents are the most important factors for the adsorption of polar organic pollutants on the polymeric adsorbent.
adsorption capacity of the polymeric resine for phenol was determined by its surface polarity and microporosity.
the microporosities and surface polarities of polymeric resines are important factors to be considered in adsorptive removal of phenol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption of organic pollutants on the polymeric adsorbent is strongly dependent on the textural parameters and surface chemistry of the polymeric resorbent.
the microporosities and surface chemistries of polymeric adsorbers should be considered in designing adsorbents for the removal of phenol from water.
the adsorption capacity of phenol could be improved by increasing the BET surface areas, the micropore volume and the surface polarity of polymeric resine.
